clue.text: Fear not, no criminal will give you time of day

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction not to be afraid, with a refusal, from a crook who will tell you the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fear not, no' looks like a reassurance, but its nine letters are what 'criminal' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between noon and evening is one of the named parts of the day.

clue.text: Fruit and a soft cheese? No thanks

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: 'No' says the following word is to be left out of the cheese

parts.note: ricotta is a soft Italian cheese
TA is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone offered fruit and soft cheese declines politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No thanks' reads as a refusal, but it tells you to drop TA (British slang for thanks) from RICOTTA, leaving RICOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small orange stone fruit related to the peach and plum.

clue.text: Twitch, seen every so often?

indicators.note: taking the letters seen only every so often from the word Twitch means its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A query about a nervous twitch that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the alternate letters of 'Twitch' spell the answer, and a recurring twitch is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual, involuntary muscle spasm that recurs from time to time.

clue.text: Banter in bar getting really heartless, sadly

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as on a fence or a towel rail

indicators.note: sadly signals that what remains is put into a sorry, jumbled state
heartless means the central pair of letters is removed from the word really

explanation.surface: Pub chat that has become cold and unfeeling, which is a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle pair of 'really', leaving RELY for 'sadly' to rearrange; 'bar' is a rail, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-humoured teasing or mockery exchanged between people is a synonym of the clue word.

clue.text: Cat's to spring, scratching Penny

indicators.note: scratching means crossing out, so a letter is struck from the word

parts.note: to pounce is to spring suddenly on prey
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A cat about to leap while clawing at someone called Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a big wild feline of Central Asian mountains, goes by this name.

clue.text: Relative adopts pose, waving part of bridle

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a niece is a relative, a sibling's daughter

indicators.note: waving suggests movement, so the letters of pose are shuffled

explanation.surface: A family member strikes a pose and waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' scrambles the four letters of 'pose', and 'adopts' takes them in just after the first letter of the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The strap of a horse's headgear that passes over the animal's nose is called this.

clue.text: Cobblers are busy gathering endorsement

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: places that hum are busy and full of activity
an OK is an endorsement or approval

explanation.surface: Shoemakers are hard at work, picking up a seal of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense, not shoe-menders here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nonsense or rubbish, the clue word being British slang.

clue.text: Delay importing European industrial interior design

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a hitch is a hold-up or delay

explanation.surface: A holdup bringing in European goods in an industrial design project.
explanation.definitionFit: A decor style using factory fittings such as exposed metal and pipework carries this label.

clue.text: Pay one keen employee finally for mending watch

indicators.note: mending means fixing or reworking, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word employee

explanation.surface: Pay a keen staff member at last for repairing a watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' looks like the timepiece being mended, but it is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep under observation or monitor something is the same as to look after it closely.

clue.text: Powerful current endlessly missing top of lightning conductor?

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool current

indicators.note: top of in a down clue points to the first letter of lightning

explanation.surface: A violent current, without the tip of a lightning rod, sounds like electrical engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests a lightning conductor, but the definition is the orchestral one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent musical conductor is often honoured with this title, meaning master.

clue.text: End of year sale doesn't start row

indicators.note: End of picks the final letter of the word year
doesn't start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an auction is a sale

explanation.surface: An end-of-year sale that fails to open leads to an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or quarrel, a row in the sense rhyming with cow.

clue.text: Drunk's present, whether you like it or not!

definitions.text: whether you like it or not!

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A defiant drunk announcing they have arrived, like it or not.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish retort of defiance, meaning that is how it is and you must accept it.

clue.text: Caught nits going round Rhodes?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nits are lice, or their eggs

explanation.surface: Someone has caught head lice that are spreading around Rhodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodes is not the Greek island but the British imperialist who founded Rhodesia.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the colonialist and mining magnate Rhodes, after whom the scholarships are named.

clue.text: Little relief provided by hot toddy perhaps?

definitions.text: Little relief provided by hot toddy perhaps?

parts.words: Little relief provided by hot toddy perhaps?
parts.note: a phrase meaning poor consolation, read literally as comfort from a cold remedy such as a hot toddy

explanation.surface: A hot whisky drink taken for a chill brings little relief.
explanation.walkthrough: A hot toddy is a traditional remedy for a cold, so the comfort it brings is literally comfort for a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meagre consolation that does little to ease a disappointment.

clue.text: Muscle contributes to surviving in the club

indicators.note: contributes to means puts itself into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: extant means still existing, surviving
a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: Strength helps someone survive as a member of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the club' is British slang for pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions describe a woman who is pregnant and awaiting a baby.

clue.text: Free beer to all? That's not bad

indicators.note: free means loosened, so the letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A round of drinks on the house for everyone is pretty good.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passable or fair is reasonably good, the sense of the phrase not bad.

clue.text: British rugby player kept consuming drug, being an idiot

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: had means kept or held
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A British rugby forward kept taking drugs, which was stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person or dunce, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Andromache romantically embraces Hector?

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: Andromache lovingly hugs her husband Hector.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend, Andromache is the wife of Hector, the Trojan champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector, the great Trojan warrior of the Iliad, is an example of a heroic figure.

clue.text: Secret or inner, primarily, put another way

definitions.text: Secret or inner, primarily, put another way

indicators.note: put another way means expressed in a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered
primarily picks the first letters of the words or and inner

explanation.surface: A definition seeking another way to say secret or inner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and also the wordplay: SECRET with O and I, the first letters of 'or inner', rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood only by a small inner circle, hence secret or private.

clue.text: Tourist on vacation eats a cold delicacy

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the next pieces go into the middle
on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of tourist remain

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker eats a chilled delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delicacy' looks like a food, but here it means sensitivity in handling people.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicacy in dealing with others, avoiding giving offence, is a synonym.

clue.text: Mexican chap accommodated by his aunt — here?

definitions.text: Mexican chap accommodated by his aunt — here?

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tia is Spanish for aunt, apt for a Mexican's aunt
Juan is a common Mexican man's name

explanation.surface: A Mexican man staying with his aunt, perhaps in a border city.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a description: Spanish for aunt houses a Mexican name, giving a place he might stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican city on the US border, a plausible home for such a man and his aunt.

clue.text: After drunken revels, rise at last to go into work?

definitions.text: After drunken revels, rise at last to go into work?

indicators.note: to go into means the shuffled letters are placed inside

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: drunken means reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order
at last points to the final letter of the word rise

explanation.surface: After a night of heavy drinking, you get up too late to go to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges the revels with E (the end of 'rise') into VERSLEE; the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep past the intended waking time, as one might after a late night.

clue.text: Slate and pine give sense of style

parts.note: to slate or pan is to criticise harshly
to ache is to pine or long for

explanation.surface: Roofing slate and pine timber lend a building flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' and 'pine' look like building materials but are verbs: criticise and yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence and stylish flair in the way something is done.

clue.text: Run down top of mountain range

indicators.note: top of in a down clue picks the first letter of mountain

parts.note: to range is to line up or align

explanation.surface: Running down from the summit of a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a line of mountains but is a verb meaning arrange in line.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage or speak ill of someone, a synonym of the phrase in its critical sense.

clue.text: Full spread's a bargain, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals the words are spoken aloud and heard as another phrase

parts.note: jam is a spread and a pact is a bargain, giving JAM PACT

explanation.surface: A generous buffet that is good value, by all accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Crammed to capacity, filled as tightly as possible.

clue.text: Daughter initially feared rabbit asking "What's up, Doc?"

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards
initially picks the first letters of feared, rabbit, asking and What's

explanation.surface: A girl was frightened by a cartoon rabbit and its catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's up, Doc?' is Bugs Bunny's catchphrase, but 'up' reverses FRAW and Doc is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is one of the seven little men in Snow White, so he is an example.

clue.text: Part of joint composition makes comeback

indicators.note: makes comeback means comes back the other way, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a nonet is a musical composition for nine players

explanation.surface: A piece of music returns to the charts as part of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The projecting piece of wood that fits into a mortise in carpentry.

clue.text: Put coat on — one's secured by a knot

indicators.note: secured by means held in place within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a node is a knot or lump
one is I, the Roman numeral, and the apostrophe S adds its S

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a coat fastened with a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like clothing, but the definition means applying a protective surface layer to metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To coat a metal with a protective oxide layer by electrolysis, a technical process.

clue.text: Short girl outside shed tears fabric

indicators.note: outside means the cut name surrounds the next piece
Short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
to cry is to shed tears

explanation.surface: A little girl outside a shed is in tears over some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is a verb, part of 'shed tears'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic textile made from a polymer fibre.

clue.text: Some money for wreath

definitions.meaning: plural of leu, the Romanian currency unit
a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the Romanian currency in the plural and a Hawaiian flower garland.

clue.text: Bruckner perhaps is new, after a fashion

indicators.note: after says the letter for new follows the word a

parts.note: the ton means fashionable society, the fashion

explanation.surface: A composer's work is novel, in its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' reads as 'somewhat', but 'after' places N after A, and TON is fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer Bruckner's forename, so Bruckner is one bearer of the name.

clue.text: Dick gets fine for first time, being out of order

indicators.note: gets means receives a new letter in exchange
for first says the new letter replaces the first occurrence

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A detective is fined for the first time for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'for first' swap F (fine) in for the first T (time) of DETECTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Faulty and not working properly, a synonym of the phrase in its broken sense.
